issues.title: Need to clarify TLS errors like authentication error
issues.author: gloinul
issues.body: In some cases errors should likely result in SCTP assocation abort. But should it always? Are there cases where a new TLS connection requrest can succeed?

comments.author: gloinul
comments.body: Likely a good solution for this is to state that if one gets a TLS error during intitial handshake if the implementation think it can address the error it should retry the TLS, otherwise it should abort the SCTP association. For rekeying one have less need to end immediately. However, at some point the key will not be appriate to use. Thus, if the TLS error is not fixible one will have to abort at some point. Else one can retry the TLS connection multiple times to attempt to fix it. However, some limit to not retry to quickly should be considered.

issues.title: Mostly Theoretical deadlock in Key Initation procedure
issues.author: gloinul
issues.body:
In the intial procedures we currently have these steps: 
`9. The server key manager receives Certificate/CertificateVerify/Finished,
   it exports the server key
   material for both the Primary and Restart DKCs, and installs it
   as its read (receive) key and as its write (send) key.

10. The server key manager calls Require Protected SCTP Packets to
    enforce DTLS chunk protection for all future packets and informs
    the ULP that the association is protected.

11. The server key manager sends a Protection Established control
    message ({{protection-established}}) to the client key manager.

12. The client key manager receives the Protection Established
    control message, exports all Primary and Restart DKC keys,
    and installs the server key material as its write (send) key,
    calls Require Protected SCTP Packets to enforce
    DTLS chunk protection for all future packets, and informs the
    ULP that the association is protected.`

In this procedure there exists a potential for deadlock that is uncertain if you even can make it trigger. But the case that exist here is the following:

When step 10 is completed the server only accepts protected packets. Then in step 11 it sends a encrypted Protection Established (PE) message to the client. At this point the client doesn't have a write key installed, only the read key. The server requires the client to send encrypted packets for them to reach the server and actually be processed. This situation lasts until the client receives the PE message, which triggers it to install the write key and also enable protection following step 12. 

So if the a SCTP packet carrying the PE message (or part of it) is lost between the server and the client, the client can't send any SACK that will actually reach the server. However, if the server does not receive the PE message its retransmission timer will fire and retransmit the non acked PE message. Thus, a true deadlock can only occur if the SCTP association at this stage would require a SACK message or some other control message to complete the transmission of the PE. 

So the question here is if this very unlikely situation needs to be addressed? 

One way of addressing this is to add additional control messages:
10. Server sends Protection Ready (Encrypted) -> Client
11. Client installs write key and sets Protection Required
12. Client sends Protection Established (Encrypted) -> Server
13. Server receives and sets Protection Required. Notifies ULP
14. Server sends Protection Established (Encrypted) -> Client
15. Client receives Protection Established, sets Protection Required and Notifies ULP

This procedure adds one RTT at minimal. Steps 14 and 15 is there to ensure that there are coordination of the ULP activation. It may be possible to skip 14 and 15 and instead have the client activate ULP at the end of step 12. But, that puts implementation requirements on server to prevent unprotected data to be delivered to ULP while delivering protected.

issues.title: Comments from Russ Housley
issues.author: teiclap
issues.body:
Here are my thought on draft-porfiri-tsvwg-sctp-dtls-handshake.

First, I want to note that draft-ietf-tls-extended-key-update, once it is finished, offers a better way to get fresh subsequent keys.  It can be used with resumption so that the TLS session does not need to be kept open.

Section 1: Use the new TLS 1.3 RFC, not the original one.

Section 3.2: It would be better to eliminate the double negative in the first sentence:

It is RECOMMENDED that only parameters marked as "Y" in the "Recommended" column of TLS registries are supported.

Section 3.4: Is "policy" the right word? It is certainly quite different that certificate policies. I wonder if you are really asking for a configuration setting.  The rekey should happen whenever the time has passed _or_ the amount of data is about to be exceeded.

Section 3.4: In the multi-homed situation, can more than one TLS session be needed by an endpoint?

comments.author: teiclap
comments.body: Section 3.4 "policy" --> "strategy"

issues.title: Improving the initial handshake procedure
issues.author: gloinul
issues.body:
During the latest meeting with  @tuexen we discussed some aspect of the draft initial procedure and potential for improvements.

Two main insights came from that discussion.
- The current process kind of assumes that the KeyManager method do understand TLS messages, i.e. need to parse them to know where TLS is in the process to trigger the right steps.
- The current process is poorly addressing if an endpoint only want to be client, and thus should be sufficient to be only using a TLS client implementation, rather than having to have both server and client. 

Thus, some exploration of improvement of how the procedure works and how it interacts with the TLS session.

comments.author: gloinul
comments.body:
In the meeting we did discuss also about the relevance for resumption of the TLS sessions. From Ericsson's perspective this is an optional feature that needs to be supported for the following performance reasons:
- Resumption results in that one don't send the whole certificate chain. This saves significant amount of message sizes, especially for the PQC certificates that is being rolled out that can be significantly bigger than any Elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman (ECDH) based ones. 
- This also saves a bit on processing and thus energy and latency. 

Session resumption tickets can be pushed by the server at any point after the handshake has completed or they could explicitly be requested by the TLS client from the TLS server. Based on this it appears that we likely will need the TLS client to be the one initiating the TLS session closure to ensure that it has had the chance to send a ticket request and the server not having prematurely closed the TLS session before it can be responded to.

comments.author: teiclap
comments.body:
There's also the need to explain that the KM is the only Client of SSID 4242, thus it offers a transport service to TLS by encapsulating its messages, furthermore in section 7 we talk about PE message in a way that is not actual anymore.
I'm going to edit all this.

issues.title: Triggering of Rekeying by server
issues.author: gloinul
issues.body:
During the discussion with @tuexen about potential improvements in regards to rekeying the important aspect was the need to not require both server and client TLS implementation when SCTP key management method has arrived at roles. Thus modification of the process should be done so that a client role should be sufficient to have only have a TLS client. This will require the server to use some other method than initiating a new TLS session to trigger the client instead initiating the TLS session. 

The suggestion we have a new key managment method level message that the server can send to the client role and have it initiate the TLS session used for rekeying.
